rootCauses.summary: The title overlay is created from mura-entry-polish, but main waits for the entire mura-enhancements graph before importing the entry surface.
rootCauses.prediction: Loading the entry surface before the enhancement graph removes heavy enhancement execution from pre-entry critical path.
rootCauses.falsifier: Immutable After still executes the full enhancement graph before the entry CTA is interactive.

rootCauses.summary: Director/crowd/visual/runtime post-boot modules execute while the player is still on the title card, producing long main-thread tasks with no gameplay benefit yet.
rootCauses.prediction: Post-entry event gating keeps those modules out of the title dwell window while preserving them after entering the village.
rootCauses.falsifier: Enhancements fail to load after entry or title-dwell long tasks remain materially unchanged.

observation.summary: Immutable village staging reaches the title, but browser evidence records severe title-dwell main-thread stalls: 96 frame samples with 44 over 50ms, p50 33.2ms, and long tasks including 7.133s while the player has not entered the village.

conditions.scenario: fresh/saved title card, no input, 3.5s dwell

evidence.statement: main awaits mura-enhancements before character runtime, interface installation and village visual language; the title surface is nested inside that enhancement graph.
The graph synchronously includes world systems, performance, experience, director, crowd and entry-polish side effects before main continues.
The entry card itself only needs the already-booted village object and currently has no post-entry lifecycle signal.

hypothesis.cause: A presentation-only title gate is placed behind a large post-boot side-effect graph, so work needed only after player intent blocks title responsiveness.
hypothesis.prediction: Move the title surface and core interface ahead of the optional enhancement graph, then trigger enhancements from a one-shot entered event. Same-condition immutable staging should show a responsive title dwell with no multi-second enhancement long task.
hypothesis.falsifier: Focused tests fail to prove ordering/event lifecycle, entering loses enhancement behavior, or After staging retains the same multi-second title dwell stall.

candidates.reason: Moves nonessential work off the title critical path without removing systems or lowering visual/gameplay quality.
Would weaken established features and quality instead of fixing lifecycle timing.
The observed stall is main-thread module/boot work; lowering visuals does not address the causal ordering.

implementation.summary: Install core interface and entry title first, dispatch a one-shot village:entered signal, and only then dynamically load post-boot enhancements/character integration/visual language.

limitations: SwiftShader timing is not a physical Pixel Fold benchmark.
Browser long-task timing can vary; lifecycle ordering is separately proven by source-level native assertions.
